decisions.decision: Validate the architecture document with Zod schemas (src/schema/) on every read and write.
decisions.rationale: The document is edited by agents, MCP tools, the CLI, and humans, so shape errors must fail loudly at the boundary rather than propagate as silent corruption. Zod gives a single declarative schema shared by readArchitecture/writeArchitecture and the MCP tools. Later history confirms the load-bearing role: ADR-0006 and f0a6a1d are built around what Zod strips (unknown keys) and must never materialise (defaults). Present since b087521; schema + semantic checks added in 69cc57a.

alternatives.name: Hand-written TypeScript type guards + manual checks
alternatives.whyNot: every new field would need a new hand-written check at every boundary (IO, MCP tools, CLI) with no single source of truth.

alternatives.name: Another validation library (io-ts, ajv)
alternatives.whyNot: unrecoverable from history — no commit, ADR, or issue discusses an alternative validator; flagged as observation, not a considered rejection.

decisions.decision: Build the server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (McpServer, stdio transport), exposing tools and architecture:// resources.
decisions.rationale: The agents arkive serves (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, and more) already speak MCP, so the SDK makes arkive a native tool/resource provider instead of a bespoke protocol each harness must learn. Added in a3e3885/3db6052/e8e0020/b7f2b84. The 7-platform auto-install (65ff3b6) only makes sense on top of this choice.

alternatives.name: Bespoke HTTP/JSON API as the agent interface
alternatives.whyNot: every harness would need custom integration code instead of MCP registration; contradicted by the arkive install <platform> direction and the architecture:// resource model.

alternatives.name: File-editing only, no server
alternatives.whyNot: no live validation, no drift checks, no prompt-queue coordination; the MCP tools are the enforcement point prose could not be (ADR-0005).

decisions.decision: Serve the viewer and JSON API over HTTP with Express (src/cli/commands/serve.ts), after the MCP server already existed over stdio.
decisions.rationale: The serve command needed static-file serving plus a small JSON API in one process alongside stdio (c900e12, after stdio-only 17eedb8). Caveat, stated plainly: the commit message states what was added, never why Express rather than anything else — the rationale is reconstructed from the code, not quoted from history.

alternatives.name: node:http only, or another framework (Fastify/Hono)
alternatives.whyNot: rationale unrecoverable from history — no commit, ADR, issue, or review discusses an alternative HTTP layer; flagged as observation.

decisions.topic: Build/bundling toolchain for the distributable package
decisions.decision: Bundle CLI, server, and library entries with tsup (cli/server/lib ESM entries, node18 target); keep Vite solely for the viewer.
decisions.rationale: The published package must run from dist/ via bin/arkive.mjs with no build step on the user machine (cf. recovered decision d1: self-contained install). tsup gives fast ESM bundling with sourcemaps per entry, which tsc alone does not. Added in 1fa2472; combined build in ecc1085.

alternatives.name: tsc-only build, no bundler
alternatives.whyNot: tsc emits per-file output with no entry-point bundling; the dist/ layout package.json assumes would have to be assembled by hand. Reconstructed, never explicitly rejected.

alternatives.name: Reuse Vite for everything
alternatives.whyNot: unrecoverable — Vite is scoped to src/viewer and no history discusses bundling the CLI with it; flagged as observation.

decisions.topic: How trust in document elements is represented
decisions.decision: Delete source/confidence scalars (shipped 61603e1, consumed 1411e8f) and require per-element provenance: {derived: true, rule, evidence[file:line]} or {derived: false, authoredBy, reviewedAt?}. No confidence field in v2.
decisions.rationale: The confidence system was inert by construction: no code path ever wrote source/confidence, so the low-confidence drift warning could fire only if an agent voluntarily followed a markdown instruction. A self-assessed scalar an LLM assigns itself is not evidence; evidence:[file:line] is. Recorded in ADR-0002, implemented in f0a6a1d; REVIEW-wave1 constrained the v2 shape (no defaults, migrated elements are authoredBy agent, never derived).

alternatives.name: Keep confidence but make it mandatory and auto-populate it
alternatives.whyNot: fixes 'nothing sets it' without fixing the defect (ADR-0002: a number an LLM assigns to itself is not evidence).

alternatives.name: Call an LLM to detect drift and propose repairs
alternatives.whyNot: decided non-goal (VISION.md non-goals); confidently wrong repairs destroy determinism, cost profile, and offline operation.

decisions.topic: How document history is retained without unbounded growth
decisions.decision: Auto-save a full-document snapshot on every write, bounded by construction: history[] capped at 50 with sticky historyTruncated, snapshots deduplicated by content hash (lastUpdated normalised out) and capped at 10 distinct states.
decisions.rationale: The durable record is git, but the working document needed recovery points, so 515f841 wrote a full copy plus history entry on every write — reproducing the context rot it cured (ADR-0002). Hence the bounds in 1099038/ADR-0006: hash-dedup stores genuine state transitions, and the cap flag keeps truncation visible, never silent.

alternatives.name: Full-copy-on-every-write with only a count cap
alternatives.whyNot: wrong mechanism — hash-dedup stores state transitions, not the same file 200 times (ADR-0006).

alternatives.name: No in-file history; git is the record
alternatives.whyNot: never explicitly rejected in history — the MCP path appends an entry per call and session-context narrates recent history, so the file won by building, not by deciding. Flagged as partially unrecoverable.

decisions.topic: Coordinating asynchronous agent work through the document
decisions.decision: A persistent prompt queue (schema + IO + HTTP endpoints + MCP prompts tool + viewer components) with actually-atomic claims: O_EXCL lock, hash compare-and-swap, claimExpiresAt lease with reapExpiredClaims.
decisions.rationale: Prompts for a future session need a durable, claimable home so two agents never execute the same work. The first implementation was an unguarded read-modify-write while README and skill claimed atomicity (59df02a/e7bb157/adbbe71/be5f32f). 1099038 made the wording true rather than deleting it, keeping the queue a human-readable file with clean contended-claim outcomes and lease recovery for dead agents (ADR-0006).

alternatives.name: Lockfile or SQLite database for the queue
alternatives.whyNot: CAS rename is already atomic on the filesystem, adds no dependency, keeps the queue human-readable; revisit only if contention ever matters (ADR-0006).

alternatives.name: Delete the 'atomically claim' wording instead of making it true
alternatives.whyNot: implicitly rejected by 1099038, which made README, tools.ts, and SKILL.md true rather than deleting them.

decisions.decision: Bundle the CLI in dist/ and publish templates and agent instructions alongside it.
decisions.rationale: RECOVERED VERBATIM from arkive/legacy-architecture.json (original id d1), orphaned at the repo root by 62066bc and restored via git mv in c4df919. Original rationale: 'Keeps the installed package self-contained for init and agent setup.' Consistent with the dist sequence 1fa2472 (tsup) to 3caa43c (install.sh) and package.json files list; plausibly authored during the 6f8523b dogfood pass.

alternatives.name: Ship only source files
alternatives.whyNot: Would require a build step after install and make the package harder to use.

decisions.decision: Bundle MCP server and web viewer in a single npm package.
decisions.rationale: RECOVERED VERBATIM from arkive/legacy-architecture.json (original id dec-002). Original rationale: 'Users want one install command, not two packages to coordinate'. Corroborated by cumulative packaging history (cbfbd60, 1fa2472, ecc1085) and quoted in the 0014 issue text. Live and contested: ADR-0004 proposes deleting the viewer from the package.

alternatives.name: Separate @arkive/server and @arkive/viewer packages
alternatives.whyNot: Adds coordination complexity and goes against user's stated preference for unified tooling.

decisions.decision: Force React 19 via Vite aliases to deduplicate with root project.
decisions.rationale: RECOVERED VERBATIM from arkive/legacy-architecture.json (original id dec-003). Original rationale: 'Viewer nested in src/viewer/ caused React 18 vs 19 duplicate, breaking hooks. Vite alias + dedupe resolves it.' Fully corroborated: 038e6f7 diff is exactly resolve.dedupe plus aliases in src/viewer/vite.config.ts:10-16; c4df919 confirms the 5 broken viewer tests had the duplicate as root cause.

alternatives.name: Pin viewer to React 18 independently
alternatives.whyNot: Would still cause duplicate React instances since root has React 19.

decisions.decision: Support both stdio (--stdio flag) and HTTP modes in serve command.
decisions.rationale: RECOVERED VERBATIM from arkive/legacy-architecture.json (original id dec-004). Original rationale: 'stdio is required for Claude Code plugin integration; HTTP is needed for the web viewer'. Corroborated: c850fa7 (--stdio flag), 17eedb8 (stdio serve), c900e12 (HTTP added, both in one command); consumers are the Claude Code plugin manifests (2463b5d) and the viewer.

alternatives.name: stdio only
alternatives.whyNot: Would prevent serving the web viewer.

alternatives.name: HTTP only
alternatives.whyNot: Claude Code plugins require stdio transport.

decisions.decision: scripts/install.sh must invoke the fully scoped $ARKIVE_PACKAGE='@ericjdz/arkive'; a test asserts no unscoped invocation survives.
decisions.rationale: A curl|bash installer running npx -y <name> executes whatever <name> resolves to. From d0c2e10 through 419cf27 until 1099038, the script ran unscoped 'npx -y arkive init' — a different npm package than @ericjdz/arkive — on the highest-trust surface in the product, with -y auto-accepting (1099038 message: dependency confusion). install.sh has no extractor so it carries no graph node; the executable record of this decision is its test, which is the subject. Evidence file: scripts/install.sh (ARKIVE_PACKAGE + ADR-0006 comment).

alternatives.name: Leave the unscoped npx -y arkive init
alternatives.whyNot: dependency confusion on a curl-pipe-bash surface; the unscoped name on the public registry is not this project.

alternatives.name: Pin by URL/tarball instead of scoped name
alternatives.whyNot: never discussed in history; flagged as observation.

decisions.decision: Delete the post-commit hook; enforce via a blocking pre-commit hook plus harness hooks (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PreCompact, Stop). No --quiet flag, no || true.
decisions.rationale: The only shipped hook (f2b9edb) installed a post-commit block running 'reconcile --quiet || true', but reconcile registers exactly one option (-d/--dir): the flag never existed, post-commit cannot block anything, and || true swallowed every failure including the criticals CI gates on. Corrective direction in ADR-0005, implemented through the fcbbb0d harness substrate; hooks stay opt-in (consent-gated installation).

alternatives.name: Keep the post-commit hook, fix the flag spelling
alternatives.whyNot: post-commit runs after the commit exists so it can never block; and any || true silences the exact failures enforcement exists to surface.

alternatives.name: Install hooks unconditionally from init
alternatives.whyNot: writing to .git/hooks unasked is an unconsented write; README claimed optionality while init installed unconditionally — fixed to opt-in.

decisions.decision: CI runs lint, test, build on Node 18/20 with pretest gating tests on lint; root tsconfig split so the node/CLI project and the src/viewer DOM/JSX project type-check separately.
decisions.rationale: v0.2.1 shipped with 659 lint errors and 7 of 56 test files failing on a clean clone, with no CI to catch it (c4df919 message). The same commit fixed two real defects the viewer noise had hidden (src/index.ts re-export of a never-exported schema; learn.ts importing undeclared open) and made package.json the single version source. The build chain (tsup + combined script) is the executable record and the subject.

alternatives.name: Keep manual pre-release checks, no CI
alternatives.whyNot: they demonstrably did not run — v0.2.1 shipped red, which is the entire evidence.

decisions.topic: Never scaffold over an existing document
decisions.decision: init probes legacy document paths first and refuses to write over an existing document (probeBlocksWrite); recovery is explicit via git mv, which preserves history.
decisions.rationale: 62066bc moved the code path from architecture.json to arkive/architecture.json but scaffolded an empty document at the new path, orphaning the real one with its four decisions at the old path (12-line diff, tests only — no data handling). Nothing warned. c4df919 recovered it via git mv to arkive/legacy-architecture.json. 1099038/ADR-0006 made the probe a first-class gate: a refused write with a loud message beats a helpful overwrite that destroys rationale.

alternatives.name: Last-write-wins scaffolding
alternatives.whyNot: silently destroys user data — demonstrated, not hypothetical; the failure the product exists to prevent, inside the product.

alternatives.name: Silent auto-merge of old and new documents
alternatives.whyNot: merging intent is a judgment call no rule can make; refusal forces explicit recovery the user can audit.

decisions.decision: Remove src/viewer's duplicate React; resolve once via Vite alias + dedupe — enforcing what dec-003 (R3) already intended.
decisions.rationale: Five viewer tests broke with hooks throwing across the React boundary because src/viewer had installed its own React alongside the root copy (c4df919 message: root cause confirmed, duplicate removed). The decision dec-003 already prescribed the dedupe; the incident is that the prescription and the tree disagreed until the tests forced the confrontation.

alternatives.name: Keep the nested React copy
alternatives.whyNot: duplicate instances break hooks across the boundary — demonstrated by the five failures, not theorised.

decisions.decision: Replace services[]/connections[] with typed nodes[]/edges[]; decided_by is a read-time projection, never stored; schemaVersion 2 with a migration chain and the v1 view kept as a derived projection.
decisions.rationale: A service list answers 'what are the pieces'; only a graph answers how they depend, what shapes flow, and which decision created each edge (VISION.md Graph layer). Specified by ADR-0001, implemented across issues 0003/0004/0008; REVIEW-wave1 corrected three ADRs in contact with implementation (binary derived/authored split, falsifiable looseObject rule, transactional writes ranked first).

alternatives.name: Extend the v1 services/connections model
alternatives.whyNot: parallel-string subjects reintroduce exactly the ambiguity discriminators remove, and edge-subject decisions are unrepresentable (REVIEW-wave1 §4; issue 0003 corrected by ADR-0002).

decisions.decision: Delete the quiz-based Learning Mode; replace it with an agent-led layered walkthrough over traversal primitives (topology/open/trace), run in the agent conversation, not the viewer.
decisions.rationale: VISION.md decided the quiz tests recall and interrogates rather than teaching; the maintainer rejected it explicitly. ADR-0003 specifies the replacement: AI chooses presentation, learner chooses destination, no script, no mastery score. The quiz also carried real defects (invented protocol options, id-derived answer positions, mastery on one correct answer). Built in 0009; deletion itself is 0015's scope.

alternatives.name: Keep the quiz alongside the walkthrough
alternatives.whyNot: VISION.md rules the framing out, and two mechanisms to learn one thing is worse than one good mechanism while the quiz defects survive.

alternatives.name: Guided-tour UI with next/prev in the viewer
alternatives.whyNot: re-creates the viewer as a product (VISION.md) and cannot express the conversational AI-presents/learner-directs split.

decisions.topic: MCP tool consolidation (nine tools to eight)
decisions.decision: Merge the prompt-queue trio into one prompts tool (list/claim/ack) and expose the walkthrough as one action-discriminated tool (topology/open/trace). The surface caps at eight tools; 0009 consolidates rather than adding a tenth.
decisions.rationale: Past about eight tools an agent reliably mis-selects; the fix is consolidation, not addition (0009 hard constraint). why_does_this_exist stays as decisionsAbout; dataShapes folds into open. The engine/handler seam (domain found:false vs transport isError) is translated at the boundary with the engine untouched.

alternatives.name: Add walkthrough as a tenth tool alongside the trio
alternatives.whyNot: grows the mis-selection surface the consolidation exists to shrink; violates the 0009 constraint.

decisions.topic: Continuous reconciliation (derive on change, diagnose on demand)
decisions.decision: Re-derive on every change (arkive watch, --apply persistence); bare reconcile is a read-only diagnostic that never rewrites the document (a test asserts the default never writes).
decisions.rationale: On-demand derivation drifts between runs; continuous derivation plus a diagnostic that cannot surprise-write is what makes the document trustworthy inside git hooks (a command that rewrote the file on every invocation could never run from a hook). Built in 0007; one scan serves drift, derivation, orphans, and authored findings.

alternatives.name: reconcile always persists
alternatives.whyNot: a command that quietly rewrites the user's architecture file on every invocation cannot run from a git hook or be read as a diagnostic.

steps.action: calls update_architecture with nodes, edges, and the decisions that explain them
validates against the v2 schema and applies the transaction (attach-at-creation, tombstone removals)
atomically writes arkive/architecture.json (temp, fsync, rename) and snapshots the state
starts the MCP server over stdio and the viewer/API over HTTP with a per-run bearer token
renders the graph from the API; prompts queued here return via the prompt queue
queues an architecture change prompt scoped to nodes
claims it via the prompts tool (atomic claim with lease) and executes it
acknowledges done/failed; reconcile and record_decision capture what changed and why

history.summary: Architecture document created
Added HTTP prompt queue endpoints to the viewer server
Updated README.md to reflect new MCP tools, resources, and prompt queue feature
Added compact session context MCP resource for token-efficient architecture retrieval
Added git hook installer and CLI command for auto-reconcile on post-commit

Recovered four decisions orphaned by the archlearn->arkive path migration: moved the stale root architecture.json to arkive/legacy-architecture.json (see docs/legacy-architecture.md) and un-ignored docs/, which had prevented the Plan 1-6 documents from ever being committed

Moved the viewer's bearer-token handoff out of a server-injected script that monkey-patched window.fetch and into the viewer itself (src/viewer/src/api/auth.ts); open_viewer now returns a fragment URL carrying the run token (docs/issues/0017-close-auth-followups.md)
Derived refresh tombstoned 2 nodes this scan could not reproduce: module:bin/arkive.mjs, module:dir:bin. Authored nodes are never removed by derivation.
0014: record authored data flows for the repository's own document
Runtime schema validation for architecture.json: Validate the architecture document with Zod schemas (src/schema/) on every read and write.
Protocol for agent-arkive communication: Build the server on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (McpServer, stdio transport), exposing tools and architecture:// resources.
HTTP server framework for serve: Serve the viewer and JSON API over HTTP with Express (src/cli/commands/serve.ts), after the MCP server already existed over stdio.
Build/bundling toolchain for the distributable package: Bundle CLI, server, and library entries with tsup (cli/server/lib ESM entries, node18 target); keep Vite solely for the viewer.

How trust in document elements is represented: Delete source/confidence scalars (shipped 61603e1, consumed 1411e8f) and require per-element provenance: {derived: true, rule, evidence[file:line]} or {derived: false, authoredBy, reviewedAt?}. No confidence field in v2.

How document history is retained without unbounded growth: Auto-save a full-document snapshot on every write, bounded by construction: history[] capped at 50 with sticky historyTruncated, snapshots deduplicated by content hash (lastUpdated normalised out) and capped at 10 distinct states.

Coordinating asynchronous agent work through the document: A persistent prompt queue (schema + IO + HTTP endpoints + MCP prompts tool + viewer components) with actually-atomic claims: O_EXCL lock, hash compare-and-swap, claimExpiresAt lease with reapExpiredClaims.
Packaging surface: Bundle the CLI in dist/ and publish templates and agent instructions alongside it.
MCP + viewer in one package: Bundle MCP server and web viewer in a single npm package.
React version for viewer: Force React 19 via Vite aliases to deduplicate with root project.
MCP transport modes: Support both stdio (--stdio flag) and HTTP modes in serve command.
curl-pipe-bash installer package identity: scripts/install.sh must invoke the fully scoped $ARKIVE_PACKAGE='@ericjdz/arkive'; a test asserts no unscoped invocation survives.
Git-hook enforcement for reconcile: Delete the post-commit hook; enforce via a blocking pre-commit hook plus harness hooks (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PreCompact, Stop). No --quiet flag, no || true.

No shipping without CI: CI runs lint, test, build on Node 18/20 with pretest gating tests on lint; root tsconfig split so the node/CLI project and the src/viewer DOM/JSX project type-check separately.

Never scaffold over an existing document: init probes legacy document paths first and refuses to write over an existing document (probeBlocksWrite); recovery is explicit via git mv, which preserves history.
Viewer dependency isolation (incident): Remove src/viewer's duplicate React; resolve once via Vite alias + dedupe — enforcing what dec-003 (R3) already intended.

Graph-first architecture document (schema v2): Replace services[]/connections[] with typed nodes[]/edges[]; decided_by is a read-time projection, never stored; schemaVersion 2 with a migration chain and the v1 view kept as a derived projection.

Walkthrough replaces quiz learning mode: Delete the quiz-based Learning Mode; replace it with an agent-led layered walkthrough over traversal primitives (topology/open/trace), run in the agent conversation, not the viewer.

MCP tool consolidation (nine tools to eight): Merge the prompt-queue trio into one prompts tool (list/claim/ack) and expose the walkthrough as one action-discriminated tool (topology/open/trace). The surface caps at eight tools; 0009 consolidates rather than adding a tenth.

Continuous reconciliation (derive on change, diagnose on demand): Re-derive on every change (arkive watch, --apply persistence); bare reconcile is a read-only diagnostic that never rewrites the document (a test asserts the default never writes).
